verdicts.reason: A: the SOLSTICE logo is tiny and pushed to the top-right corner off the centre line. The headline sits below a lone oversized can. The three flavour names are stacked in reverse order and cut off from their descriptors, which are listed below in an order that doesn't match. The middle text block is jammed while the two small cans at the bottom are a different size from the hero can. B repeats the same broken flavour block and adds worse problems: the logo is buried as a speck at the very bottom, and the CTA has shrunk to a small left-aligned pill crowded against the ONLINE ONLY badge, so the call to action is weak and the brand is almost lost.

A has the better reading order: the logo and a large headline come first, then the copy, the product and the CTA. But the flavour names are still separated from their mismatched descriptors. The CTA is undersized and jammed beside the ONLINE ONLY badge, and the two bottom cans are wildly different sizes, which looks accidental. B (the same layout as pair 1A) has a full-width CTA, but the headline is demoted to the middle under the hero can, the logo is tiny in the top-right corner, and the copy stack is cramped with the same broken name and descriptor pairing.

A runs in a sensible order (brand, headline, copy, cans, then a large prominent CTA), but the flavour names and descriptors are still split and mismatched. The two small cans float next to the large can at inconsistent sizes, and the ONLINE ONLY badge is jammed under the CTA, nearly touching it. B (identical to 1A) puts the headline below the hero can and has a tiny corner logo, a cramped middle text stack and the same scrambled flavour list, so its hierarchy and brand presence are weaker.
